adhimokkha.p: [Adhi+mukha+kha] (pu) CL=9 Dhanti. 159 and see sūci] Determination; The Dhamma of determination, decision making. (1) Nature of determination of the object whether it is right or wrong, Adhimokkhacetasika. (2) Strong faith which makes its associated dhammas very pleased/serene, Adhimokkha comprising in the ten imperfections of insight.

(c) bear in mind
(2) especially free from lust., defilements
A monk named adhimutta
[PMED]
pn:
Adhimutta 01. A Brahmin of Sāvatthī. Dissatisfied with Brahmin learning, he looked for salvation elsewhere, and hearing the Buddha preach at the presentation of Jetavana, entered the Saṅgha, becoming an Arahant in due course (Thag-a.i.224). A verse addressed by him to some corpulent monks is found in the Theragāthā (v.114).

In Padumuttara’s time he was a learned Brahmin and became an ascetic. Later he met the Buddha, offered him a bark-robe and uttered his praises in song. He is probably identical with Sabbakittika of the Apadāna (i.323-4).
